summary: At the bodega, Bjorn finds no debt to repay and no labor to perform; the owner simply gives him his usual coffee and lets ordinary familiarity be enough.
settingText: Recurring bodega front counter during a quiet morning lull.
panelPlan: bodega front counter — Wide: The store is quiet between customers. The Bodega Owner pours Bjorn's usual coffee while Bjorn automatically scans the aisle, delivery stack and counter for work that might need doing.
bodega front counter — Two-shot: The owner notices Bjorn looking past him toward the back aisle and slides the coffee across.
bodega counter — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn takes the cup but continues looking around the shop as if a task must be hiding somewhere.
bodega counter — Two-shot: The owner leans one forearm on the counter and asks about the promotional toaster. Bjorn finally looks at him instead of at the work.
bodega front counter — Wide: Bjorn stands drinking coffee while the owner checks a receipt. Neither man needs anything from the other for the moment.

summary: Carrie arrives to escort Bjorn to the next meeting and learns he already left alone because Gunnar showed him the route once.
settingText: Apartment doorway, Safe Cave interior and a brief view of the block outside.
panelPlan: fifth-floor hallway at apartment 5B — Medium: Carrie knocks once and enters with her coat still on, one hand already gesturing back toward the hallway as she calls for Bjorn.

Safe Cave interior — Wide: Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin tightens a strap on a household bag. Bjorn, Astrid and Second Male Kin are absent; after Carrie calls, neither Gunnar nor First Male Kin looks toward the door.
Safe Cave table — Medium on Carrie and Gunnar: Carrie scans the empty window and sleeping side of the studio where Bjorn would normally be, then looks back to Gunnar.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Carrie points her thumb toward the hallway as she asks whether Bjorn left alone. Gunnar turns one page before replying.

Bushwick sidewalk half a block from apartment — Long medium: Bjorn walks alone half a block from the apartment through ordinary pedestrian traffic, coat closed and pace steady toward the community center.

summary: At the next meeting, the 1987 Participant asks about a family dinner; Bjorn stops before deciding for them, asks what they actually want, and offers a boundary and an exit instead of a verdict.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during Bjorn's next support-group meeting.
panelPlan: Wide: The next meeting is already underway. The 1987 Participant sits across from Bjorn; the facilitator is visible in the same ordinary chair as everyone else.
Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant describes the family dinner problem with irritation rather than panic.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn starts to answer immediately, stops after two words, then resets and asks a different question.
Two-shot: The participant answers without looking at the facilitator. Bjorn listens through the whole sentence.
Two-shot: Bjorn gives the narrowest advice he can: state the boundary before arriving and leave if the bargain changes.
Close on participant then Bjorn: The participant asks whether that means they should go. Bjorn refuses to turn the boundary into a command.

dialogueInline.text: My brother wants me at dinner. Last time they asked about music and Reagan all night.
If they do it anyway, leave.

summary: The 1987 Participant points out that either choice can still hurt; Bjorn admits he cannot make the decision painless, learning that respecting agency does not guarantee a clean outcome.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room during the same meeting.
panelPlan: Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant does not let Bjorn's boundary advice end the problem.
Two-shot: Bjorn listens. The facilitator watches from the side without stepping in.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn looks down for a beat instead of producing a faster answer.
Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant pushes because the answer is unsatisfying.
Two-shot: Bjorn accepts the inadequacy of his answer rather than turning it into an order.
Wide: The participant leans back and makes their own choice. Bjorn nods once; the facilitator says nothing.

dialogueInline.text: If I leave, my brother thinks I rejected them. If I stay, I become the story again.
I don't know how to make it cheaper.
Then I go. If it starts, I leave.

summary: After the meeting, Bjorn and the facilitator agree that adults need ways to contribute and clash over whether contribution should ever become the price of care.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during cleanup, then hallway.
panelPlan: community-center multipurpose room after meeting — Wide: Participants stack cups and chairs. Bjorn folds one chair and adds it to the same stack while two other participants clean nearby.
community-center multipurpose room — Two-shot: Bjorn and the facilitator continue their argument while carrying chairs toward the wall.
community-center multipurpose room — Medium on facilitator: The facilitator keeps carrying a folded chair toward the wall while answering Bjorn.
community-center multipurpose room — Two-shot: Bjorn stops his folded chair against the wall and turns to face the facilitator. The facilitator sets their own chair beside it while answering him.
community-center hallway — Wide: They walk in opposite directions down the hallway, both still wearing tight, irritated expressions.

dialogueInline.text: If nobody needs you, what do you do all day?
If people feed you and ask nothing—

summary: Carrie vents about a DTI deadline mess, and Bjorn asks whether she wants counsel or only a witness before offering any solution.
settingText: Neighborhood coffee cart and nearby sidewalk bench in late afternoon.
panelPlan: sidewalk beside neighborhood coffee cart — Medium: Carrie walks beside Bjorn with coffee and a folder tucked under one arm, already mid-rant.
sidewalk beside coffee cart — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn walks beside Carrie with brows knit, eyes fixed on her and both hands empty and still while she continues.
sidewalk — Two-shot: Bjorn raises one hand slightly and asks his question before Carrie reaches the next complaint.
sidewalk — Two-shot: Carrie stops for half a step and turns to look directly at Bjorn. He meets her eye and repeats the question.
sidewalk walking away from coffee cart — Two-shot: They resume walking. Carrie says “Witness.” Bjorn delivers one sentence, then goes silent while she answers “Thank you.”

dialogueInline.text: He changed the deadline, emailed me the old one, then asked why I was confused.
Now I have to explain dates to a man with three calendars.
You want me to fix it?
You want me to say he's an idiot?
